entries.caption_draft: Data coverage and arrival/dwell calibration. (a) Share of five-minute slots observed per site-day; open cells are missing days. (b) Dwell-time histogram with the fitted distribution. (c) Hold-out check of the fitted arrival/dwell model on held-out site-days.

Service rate against the integer number of equipped berths k. Solid line: mean over replayed site-days; band: 95% interval from the site-day bootstrap. Dashed line: tolerance alpha; filled marker: selected k under the risk-margin rule. Open chevron: search range ended before the tolerance was met (grid truncated, not infeasible).

Feasible configuration set and minimality class per site-rule cell. (a) Minimality class of the smallest admissible k, one cell per site x rule. (b) Class counts over the enumerated grid; the empty-set and truncated-range counts are reported next to the bars rather than merged.

Independent-test performance of the allocation rules and the baseline set. Points are means over held-out site-days with 95% interval bars; the dashed line is the tolerance. B0 FCFS, B1 fixed quota and B2 literature-adapted are baselines; B2 is offline and not online executable where flagged.

Change in the smallest admissible k on each independent stream when the charging-intention field is added (condition I1 vs I0). (a) Paired k per stream, sorted by delta k; a negative delta means fewer equipped berths are needed under I1. (b) Service trade-off per stream; points off the y=0 line are cases where the signal changes the service rates as well as k. Exploratory result, not a value-of-information estimate.

Energy feasibility against the number of equipped berths, charger power and the site feeder. (a) Energy shortfall rate on the k x power grid at the smallest tested feeder; the white line marks the feasible boundary and the chevrons mark the feeder-limited edge. (b) Shortfall against charger power for three feeder sizes at the selected k; points to the right of a feeder's limit are capped, not measured.

Event trajectory on one selected instance where one extra equipped bay lowers ICEV parking failures. (a) Equipped bays in use over the operating window under k and k-1; hatching marks the extra bay. (b) Cumulative failures under the two configurations; the ICEV curve of k sits below that of k-1 while the EV curve is above it, which is the non-monotone response reported in the text.
